genZNote: The one classic dermatophyte genus that never touches hair — skin and nails only, no microconidia needed to make the point.

morphology.shape: Septate hyphae with smooth-walled, club/banana-shaped macroconidia in clusters; no microconidia

reproductiveStructures: Smooth-walled, club/banana-shaped macroconidia in clusters (no microconidia produced)

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human skin and nails (anthropophilic — exclusively human-associated, unlike Microsporum/Trichophyton which have zoophilic/geophilic members)
habitat.hostAssociation: Anthropophilic dermatophyte — transmitted person-to-person or via fomites
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Survives on shared surfaces such as locker room floors, shower stalls, and shared towels

microscopy.stain: KOH wet mount; lactophenol cotton blue of culture
microscopy.appearance: Septate hyphae; smooth-walled, club-shaped macroconidia in clusters, no microconidia present

culture.media: Sabouraud dextrose agar, dermatophyte test medium (DTM)
culture.growthCharacteristics: Obligate aerobe; grows over 1-2 weeks; turns DTM red
culture.colonyMorphology: Khaki to olive-green, suede-like to powdery surface, often with radial folds

identificationClues: Never produces microconidia — only smooth-walled, club/banana-shaped macroconidia in clusters, a key genus-defining feature
Does not infect hair (no ectothrix or endothrix invasion), unlike Microsporum and Trichophyton
Khaki/olive-green, suede-like colonies with radial folds
Common cause of tinea cruris ('jock itch') and tinea pedis

virulenceFactors: Keratinase enzymes allowing invasion of skin and nail keratin (does not invade hair keratin)
clinicalImportance.transmission: Person-to-person or fomite contact (shared towels, locker room floors, shower stalls)
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: A classic cause of tinea cruris, often occurring alongside tinea pedis in the same patient (autoinoculation from feet to groin); exclusively anthropophilic, so outbreaks track close-contact/shared-facility settings
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Absence of microconidia on culture combined with lack of hair invasion helps distinguish E. floccosum from Trichophyton and Microsporum species

examFacts.shape: Septate hyphae, club-shaped macroconidia, no microconidia
examFacts.importantTest: Culture morphology — macroconidia only, no microconidia, no hair invasion
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: The only classic dermatophyte genus that never produces microconidia and never invades hair — skin and nails only
